newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - June 19.

text.p: Sowry wants allegations probed: Social Welfare Minister Roger Sowry offered on Wednesay night to cooperate with any independent investigation of complaints that Social Welfare Department staff in Auckland had falsified death certificates of children in care. Page 1.

Expect 'damn good Budget' says PM: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Wednesday promised "a damn good Budget" next Thursday, having earlier warned business leaders not to expect "the second coming". Page 2.

Tension rife after Banks's boycott of 'flash party': Tensions between maverick National MP John Banks and his NZ First colleagues surfaced in Parliament on Thursday, the day after he boycotted a joint caucus meeting aimed at patching up strained coalition relations. Page 2.

Call for register of MPs' finances: All MPs should be required to publicly declare all their financial interests to ensure they were not unduly influenced by outside interests, senior National backbencher Tony Ryall said on Wednesday. Page
Price plunge rocks Petrochem: The "Think Big" Petrochem fertiliser plan in Taranaki is laying off 35 staff and asking others to take pay cuts of up to 18 percent. Page 19.
BT to gain in takeover of Wellington sharebroker: Bankers Trust New Zealand's purchase of Wellington-based institutional sharebroker Doyle Paterson Brown looks set to benefit both firms. Page 19.

Ansett, Air NZ freight to merge: Air New Zealand and Ansett Australia Holdings are going to merge their New Zealand domestic air freight and courier busiensses: Air NZ First Express and Ansett NZ Air Freight. Page 19.
Bank cautions against overstating economic gloom: Economic confidence has weakened recently but the ANZ bank has warned against too much pessimism. Page 19.

Used car import orders called off: Orders for thousands of used cars due to be imported from Japan have been cancelled -- and some in the industry claimed it was because the cars had been tampered with.

MP fails to show evidence: The deputy leader of ACT, Ken Shirley, failed to produce evidence to back up his claims that child welfare staff had falsified legal documents when he met the Minister of Social Welfare, Roger Sowry, late on Wednesday night.

Titans set to cross swords: Greame Hart and Sir Ronald Brierley, two titans of the New Zealand market, are set to cross swords once again, this time in Australia. The pair are headed for a legal battle.
Shark victim will survive, but loses leg: A Christchurch woman attacked by a shark in Fiji has won her desperate fight for life, but lost part of her badly bitten leg. Page 1.

MPs stand firm against scrapping differential: South Island MPs remain resolute in their opposition to the removal of the NZ$10.9 million power price differential after meeting at Parliament on Wednesday. Page 3.

Infratil, NZ Post qualify for bid: A group including New Zealand Post and infrastructure investment company Infratil International is among three groups which have qualified to bid for a 30-year consession to run the State-owned Argentine Post Office. Page 31.

Colliers ownership shuffle: Colliers Macaulay Nicolls, a member of the worldwide Colliers International Group, has offered to buy 50 percent of the Colliers Jardine Group for an undisclosed cash sum. Page 31.
